claims.text: Equimolar CoCrFeNiTi has relatively low hardness and strength despite favorable plasticity and machinability.
The relatively low hardness and strength are primarily governed by a soft, disordered, single-phase structure.
The single-phase CoCrFeNiTi structure provides limited solid-solution strengthening.
Nanoscale compositional fluctuations are present in equimolar CoCrFeNiTi.
The nanoscale compositional fluctuations do not sufficiently obstruct dislocation motion.
Conventional casting and homogenization produce a fine-grained, simple solid-solution state in equimolar CoCrFeNiTi.
Severe plastic deformation followed by low-temperature annealing can alter nanoscale compositional fluctuations, short-range order, or precipitation in CoCrFeNiTi.
Nanoscale compositional fluctuations or incipient short-range order provide only limited hindrance to dislocation motion in the single-phase alloy.
Structural disorder enables facile dislocation glide and thereby promotes high ductility.
The absence of precipitates or significant local ordering produces lower hardness and yield strength.
Enhancing nanoscale compositional modulation should increase strength and hardness at the cost of some ductility.
Reducing nanoscale compositional fluctuations should further improve ductility while producing only marginal strength gains.
Changes in nanoscale order should correlate with measurable changes in hardness and strength.
The proposed property relationships apply from ambient temperature to 600 °C under conventional quasi-static loading.
